title: Injectivity modulo the maximal ideal into a flat module (Noetherian local)
statement: Let $\varphi:(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ be a local homomorphism of local rings (commutative rings with exactly one maximal ideal; $\varphi(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$) with $S$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $M$ be an $R$-module which is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], let $N$ be a finite $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], regarded as an $R$-module via $\varphi$, and let $u:N\to M$ be an $R$-linear map. If the induced map $\bar u:N/\mathfrak mN\to M/\mathfrak mM$ is injective, then $u$ is injective and the $R$-module $M/u(N)$ is flat.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ME (lemma-mod-injective, line 23424), proof lines 23436-23477 (Krull intersection theorem, Lemma lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero; flatness via Tor, Lemma lemma-characterize-flat). Tag verified in tags/tags: 00ME,algebra-lemma-mod-injective

proof.text: For a module X annihilated by the maximal ideal, identify N tensor X and M tensor X with their residue quotients tensor X. Tensoring the injective residue map over the residue field is injective. This is the proved private helper rTensor_injective_of_maximal_annihilates.

Induct on n for modules annihilated by the nth power. Use the exact sequence mX → X → X/mX → 0, tensor right exactness for N, and injectivity of mX tensor M → X tensor M by flatness. The two tensor maps on mX and X/mX are injective by induction and the preceding step. A diagram chase proves injectivity on X.

For finite X over R, a kernel element in N tensor X maps to zero after tensoring X → X/m^n X, so lies in m^n(N tensor X) for every n. N tensor X is finite over S, via the base-change tensor equivalence. Transfer membership to (mS)^n(N tensor X) and use Krull intersection because mS lies in the Jacobson radical.
Apply the preceding tensor injectivity to X=R/J (a cyclic R-module) for every ideal J. The tensor-quotient equivalences imply u(x) in JM only if x is in JN. At J=0 this proves injectivity of u.

Prove flatness of C=M/range u by the ideal tensor criterion, adapting Module.Flat.quotient_range from WeilConjectures.Mathlib.RingTheory.Filtration to distinct domain N and codomain M. Lift z in C tensor J to y in M tensor J. Its multiplication image lies in range u, say u(x); purity gives x in JN, so lift x to yprime in N tensor J. Injectivity of the multiplication map for flat M gives y=u tensor J(yprime). The quotient map kills this image, hence z=0. All these steps are written in the proved private helper flat_quotient_range_of_ideal_preimage.
